name: elevenlabs
summary: Successfully completed the ElevenLabs quickstart end-to-end. Installed the elevenlabs and python-dotenv packages, created a Python script that calls the text-to-speech API with the provided ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, and generated a valid MP3 audio file (output.mp3, 44.1 kHz, 128 kbps, mono, ~2.77 seconds). Verified the file with ffprobe confirming it is a proper MPEG audio file.
deviations: The quickstart example uses `from elevenlabs.play import play` and `play(audio)` to play audio through speakers. Since the sandbox has no speakers and MPV was not installed, I used `from elevenlabs import save` and `save(audio, "output.mp3")` instead to save the audio to a file and verify it. This is a functionally equivalent outcome — text-to-speech successfully generated an audio file from text.

env_ready.evidence: pip install elevenlabs python-dotenv exited 0, confirming Python and pip were available and functional

configured.evidence: python example.py exited 0 and produced audio, proving ELEVENLABS_API_KEY was present and loaded via load_dotenv/os.getenv as scripted

verified.evidence: output.mp3: Audio file with ID3 version 2.4.0, contains: MPEG ADTS, layer III, v1, 128 kbps, 44.1 kHz, Monaural

friction.where: Quickstart code example assumes local playback
